questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have much family all over the UK. Furthermore, I have always wanted to live in the UK for a period of time to experience any similarities and disparities with my native culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Through the platform of Mobility Online along with both mails from my home Universities' Study Abroad team, as well as the University of Bristol's team, made all relevant information easily accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a very informative introduction meeting orchestrated by the Study Abroad team at Bristol University as well as socials they arranged for the international students with goal of making us mingle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very fortunate that the University of Bristol offers a lot of different forms of off Campus accommodation. I applied for a room through their website and got one.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There can be travel time involved getting to and from Campus, especially if you live in the North Residential Village in Bristol. Also, on Bank Holidays the bus service is either limited or cancelled, which is also worth noting for getting to and from the city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At the host University, I had to register online through their website. I did this by typing in my surname, date of birth and my assigned student number, that I had received in a mail from the University of Bristol.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was specifically told where to register and by when in an email from the Study Abroad team at the University of Bristol.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted, and there was a good connection between Mobility Online and the end result of the courses I had at the University of Bristol.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep looking out for emails! Do not be afraid to write emails back to the host Universities. They are usually quite helpful!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three courses as electives that 3rd year students of the BA were eligible for choosing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was seminars, that are similar to back home, and then lectures. The lectures were new, brief and was used as preparation for the weekly seminar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOCI30097_2022_TB-2: Modern Slavery: Issues and Debates 2022

SOCI30062_2022_TB-2: Perspectives on Power 2022

POLI31381_2022_TB-2: The Politics of Post Apartheid South Africa 2022

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend courses that are at least one year below what they would normally choose in their native country, because it can be difficult to adapt to a system in which the sole language is English.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was quite expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were different clubs for almost any activity: dancing, archery, fencing and the like. However, these clubs were also known as societies and they were not easy to get into as a foreign student due to bureaucratic processing of application for membership.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the language café where it is possible to speak all kinds of languages with other students studying abroad.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going on more trips than I have done. Cardiff is only 50 minutes away, Bath is even closer, and both are reportedly worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I started drinking way more, but apart from that, the culture was fairly similar to Denmark, and therefore the adjustment was easy enough.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Pay attention to local students, do not come on too strong, but act interested in what they have to say. Meet them where they are and be easy-going.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that partying is a part of the weekdays was hard for me to manage.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the food culture here as well as a more welcoming view on cultural and ethnic differences. Bristol is a very inclusive city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Things are not cheaper. 
Time will fly by in a blink, so try to live in the moment. 
Say yes to strangers more than no - put in the time for social activities. It pays off.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Flying to Bristol is way more expensive than flying to London and taking a coach from there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The sense of independence I achieved and the social network of people I created on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language, on certain days I found myself finding it difficult to express myself in English, and other days it was way easier. It fluctuated.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
